needs_review: UNBLOCKED by two Spec v1.1 runtime features, both re-read in the code rather than taken on trust. (1) base_url uses {{suffix api_key -}}, which renders ONLY the part of the key after its last hyphen, so a key ending -us21 routes to us21.api.mailchimp.com exactly as integrationTypeRegistry's own testEndpoint does (api_key.split('-').pop()). declarativeRuntime suffixOf returns undefined when the value has no separator, and never falls back to the whole field, so the key body cannot reach a hostname, a DNS query or a TLS SNI record. (2) auth uses userLiteral 'anystring' with passField api_key, which is the documented scheme verbatim (curl -u "anystring:APIKEY"). No vault change was needed: the mailchimp type's single api_key field carries the datacenter itself.

an earlier revision of this draft recorded these as BLOCKERS and shipped zero tools. That was correct against the runtime as it stood when first read and is now stale: specSchema checkToken accepts {{suffix <credentialField> <sep>}} in base_url.template, and checkAuth accepts userLiteral as the exclusive alternative to userField. The reversal is recorded here rather than silently overwritten.

base_url._probe is an object of CREDENTIAL-FIELD overrides used only when rendering base_url for a blind probe ({"api_key": "probekeybody-us1"} makes the suffix helper yield us1), NOT a host or URL string. connector-shapeproof.mjs baseUrlProbeValues iterates Object.entries(_probe) and strips a cred. prefix, so a string there would enumerate into per-character keys, leave api_key unfilled, and the spec would come back unprobeable. The probe value is a throwaway literal with no key body in it.

PROVEN by this run (mailchimp.proof.json, overall SHAPE_PROVEN): the suffix helper renders a real Mailchimp datacenter host, us1.api.mailchimp.com resolves and serves TLS, and the modelled routes answer with Mailchimp's own structured error JSON (type/title/status/detail), distinguishable from the control probe at a bogus path on the same host. The basic-auth wire format is accepted as a wall, not as a malformed request.

UNPROVEN, and it stays unproven until a real key runs: every response pick. The probe fires a dummy credential, so no 2xx body was ever data, and picks are taken from the official Marketing API reference pages (ping health_status; lists[] with nested stats.member_count / open_rate / click_rate; campaigns[] with nested settings.title, settings.subject_line and recipients.list_id; lists/{list_id}/members[]; the single-campaign object). A wrong pick source yields silently empty output rather than an error, so the first real run must confirm the field names.

UNPROVEN: that 'anystring' is accepted as the username. Mailchimp documents it, and the wall answered structurally, but a dummy key is rejected under any username, so this run cannot distinguish a username Mailchimp accepts from one it ignores.

count is clamped 10 default / 50 max on all three list tools, below Mailchimp's documented 1000 ceiling, to keep one tool result inside the 2000-char truncate. Callers cannot page: offset is deliberately not exposed, so these tools answer 'what does this account look like' and never enumerate an audience.

READ-ONLY: no tool is marked write:true, and every request is a GET. Mailchimp's POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE surface (members, campaigns, automations, sending) is extensive and none of it is modelled; adding any of it needs an explicit write review.
rate limit 30 requests per 60s is a self-imposed connector budget, not Mailchimp's published limit (Mailchimp documents 10 concurrent connections per key and does not publish a fixed per-minute cap).
